MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 4 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Malampaya Source: Prime Energy Prime Energy Resources Development (Prime Energy), a subsidiary of Prime Infrastructure Capital, has brought fresh natural gas reserves online from deepwater Palawan to power the Luzon grid and strengthen national energy independence off the coast of the Philippines. The Malampaya Phase 4 (MP4) project has achieved its first gas milestone, bringing natural gas from the Malampaya East-1 and Camago-3 wells into the existing Malampaya production system and extending the productive life of the field. Prime Energy describes this achievement as a significant milestone for the Malampaya consortium that reinforces the project’s role in sustaining the Philippines’ indigenous natural gas supply. President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., together with Department of Energy (DOE) officials and SC 38 joint venture partners, witnessed the ceremonial first flow of gas at the Malampaya onshore gas plant in Batangas City on November 5. MP4 was completed in 27 months after the final investment decision, approximately five months ahead of its original schedule, and five months ahead of the industry benchmark, reflecting the strong coordination across the project, particularly given the complexity of deepwater development, which involved multiple contractors and suppliers and required the mobilization of specialized equipment, manufactured components, and technical experts from around the world. articles.body: Brent Oil Prices Prepare for Biggest Weekly Drop Since 2020 After US Midterms Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 6, 2026 © Adobe Stock/le Oil prices were set for a sharp weekly fall after the election losses of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party raised hopes of a de-escalation in the US-Israeli war on Iran and a stock market sell-off, though attacks on vessels in the Middle East continue to provide a floor to crude. In a whiplash see-saw session on Friday, Brent crude futures for January were up 26 cents, or 0.3%, at $98.55 a barrel by 1346 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures edged up by 57 cents, or 0.6%, to $91.09. The Brent contract is on track for a 16% decline this week, which would be its steepest weekly percentage fall since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and its biggest in absolute terms in LSEG data going back to 1988. WTI is set for a 13% decline. The oil price slide comes against the backdrop of a dramatic rout in technology stocks. MKTS/GLOB A potential Iran war de-escalation could lead to more crude exports out of the region. Signs of an emerging supply excess amid demand destruction were reinforced by spot premiums for Middle Eastern crude benchmarks returning to levels reached before the conflict. “The crude market is loosening to a state of oversupply based on the balance, but the quality difference still exists as refiners recover what they can take versus what is available," said Rystad oil market analyst Janiv Shah, pointing to longer voyages and the need for ship-to-ship transfers as workarounds near Hormuz. "The market is still looking for evidence of a firm deal being signed (on Iran), or any backlash from either party could tighten fundamentals once more.” Oil prices fell 8% on Wednesday alone after the Democrats swept the US midterm elections, settling at two-month lows. However, prices rebounded on a surge in tanker attacks in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, renewing concerns over supply flows from the region. A Greek ship manager said on Friday that a seafarer was killed in a November 5 explosion on an oil products tanker in the Gulf, believed to have been caused by a missile attack. Data from Britain's maritime security agency UKMTO suggested that attacks on oil-carrying ships are still running at close to record pace. "Oil doesn't have to be at $117 to be expensive, and a fall to $93 doesn't mean the underlying problems have disappeared," said Matt Stanley from tanker trackers and energy flow analysts Kpler. "After over 25 years in this business, I honestly can't recall many weeks quite like this one." (Reuters)

articles.body: Pipes November 6, 2026 · 1 day ago Tubular package provider selected for first commercial gas project off Cyprus NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Tenaris Luxembourg-headquartered Tenaris has secured contracts to supply oil country tubular goods (OCTG), line pipe and coating services for Cyprus's first-ever commercial gas development, operated by Eni in partnership with TotalEnergies. The deepwater Cronos project, located in Block 6, will be developed through a fast-track approach leveraging existing regional infrastructure. With resources estimated at more than 3 trillion cubic feet (85 billion cubic meters) of gas initially in place, the project is expected to reach a production plateau of up to 500 million standard cubic feet (14.2 million cubic meters) per day. The final investment decision (FID) was reached on July 28, and start-up is expected in H1 2028. Gas produced from the field will be transported to Egypt, where it will be processed through existing facilities, including the Zohr infrastructure, before being liquefied at the Damietta LNG plant for export to international markets, primarily Europe. Tenaris will deliver a coordinated supply scope for line pipe and OCTG solutions, supporting both the transportation infrastructure and offshore drilling requirements, and will supply seamless pipes for a 110-kilometer gas export pipeline and a monoethylene glycol (MEG) pipeline. The project will be executed under Tenaris’s One Line service model, which integrates pipe manufacturing, coating and logistics in a comprehensive pipeline solution. The seamless pipes will be manufactured at the company's Dalmine mill in Italy and supplied with buckle arrestors, as well as TenarisShawcor three-layer polypropylene (3LPP) anticorrosion coating applied at the company’s coating facility in Italy. For the offshore drilling scope, Tenaris will supply all tubular requirements. Part of the order will incorporate Dopeless technology, a mill-applied multifunctional coating, which the company says is designed to eliminate the need for thread compounds and simplify pipe handling and preparation while providing consistent lubrication during offshore running operations. “Being selected to provide OCTG together with offshore line pipe for Cronos demonstrates the value of our integrated tubular offering and our ability to support customers across different stages of complex offshore developments," said Alessandro D’Angelo , Commercial Vice President for OCTG Europe, C.I.S. and Sub-Saharan Africa. articles.body: Asia Dry Cargo Khalid Hashim set to pass the baton at Precious Shipping Adis Ajdin November 6, 2026 0 705 1 minute read Thailand’s Precious Shipping is preparing a change at the top, with longtime managing director Khalid Moinuddin Hashim moving to executive vice chairman and finance chief Gautam Khurana taking over the running of the Bangkok-listed dry bulk owner. The company’s board approved the leadership reshuffle, with both appointments taking effect on January 1, 2027, according to a filing with the Stock Exchange of Thailand. Khurana will continue to serve as director of finance until a successor is appointed. Both executives will retain their seats on the company’s board of directors and executive board. The transition marks a significant shift for Precious Shipping, which has been led by Hashim for more than three decades. He helped build the company into one of Thailand’s most prominent dry bulk owners following its establishment in 1989 and stock market listing in 1993. Khurana joined Precious in 2018 as chief financial officer before becoming finance director in 2019. His earlier career included a decade at DVB Bank in London and Singapore, where he worked in maritime finance, structured asset financing and leasing. The management shake-up comes amid a major fleet renewal programme that has seen Precious sell ageing handysize and supramax vessels while expanding its ultramax fleet. In September, the company returned to China’s Taizhou Sanfu Ship Engineering for four 64,500 dwt ultramax newbuildings worth a combined $141.8m, with deliveries scheduled between April 2030 and January 2031. The order followed an earlier $133.46m contract for four 63,500 dwt ultramaxes at the same yard, with two vessels already in service and the remaining pair due through the first quarter of 2027. Once the outstanding newbuildings arrive, Precious expects its fleet to reach 47 vessels totalling about 2.34m dwt. The owner has also started diversifying beyond dry bulk, entering the MR product tanker market earlier this year through direct acquisitions and its 45%-owned Nusantara Maritime joint venture. articles.body: Europe Tech Alfa Laval makes $700m NAVTOR bet Adis Ajdin November 6, 2026 0 498 2 minutes read Alfa Laval Alfa Laval Swedish industrial group Alfa Laval has struck a $700m all-cash deal to acquire Norwegian maritime software specialist NAVTOR, significantly expanding a digital shipping portfolio that already includes StormGeo and Portchain. The Stockholm-listed group has entered into a definitive agreement to buy NAVTOR for SEK6.85bn ($700m), with completion expected during the first quarter of 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. Alfa Laval described the purchase as one of the most significant transactions in its history. NAVTOR will join its Ocean Division, with its platform set to be brought together with StormGeo and Portchain to create a broader digital fleet offering spanning navigation, vessel performance, voyage optimisation and port operations. NAVTOR, founded in Egersund in 2011, employs around 400 people across 13 offices and serves customers in more than 90 countries. Alfa Laval said it expects the business to generate about $194m in revenue this year. “With this acquisition, Alfa Laval will expand its digital offering at a time when real-time decision-making is increasingly complex,” said chief executive Tom Erixon. NAVTOR has grown from an electronic navigation specialist into a wider ship-to-shore software business covering voyage planning, fleet monitoring, vessel performance, digital logbooks and onboard data workflows. Its expansion has also been driven by acquisitions. US technology investor Accel-KKR took a majority stake in NAVTOR in 2020, followed by purchases of performance analytics specialist Tres Solutions in 2021 and digital logbook developer Ingenium Marine in 2022. NAVTOR then combined with Voyager Worldwide in 2023, creating a business whose technology at the time served about 18,000 vessels. Alfa Laval has been assembling its own maritime software stack since buying weather routing and voyage optimisation company StormGeo for NOK3.63bn in 2021. That buildout accelerated again last week when StormGeo acquired Copenhagen-based Portchain, whose network links shipping lines with more than 200 container terminals accounting for over 40% of global container terminal capacity. The technology is being combined with StormGeo’s voyage optimisation tools so vessel speed and arrival decisions can respond to changing berth availability. NAVTOR brings another major layer to that strategy. SplashTech reported only last week that the company had added near-live AIS streaming to NavFleet, while earlier this year it expanded its digital logbook and compliance tools. Alfa Laval also disclosed that a recent NAVTOR internal review identified unspecified compliance matters, prompting the Norwegian company to strengthen its internal controls and compliance programme. The buyer said arrangements have been made to protect it against pre-acquisition liabilities connected with those matters. Erixon said Alfa Laval was confident the issues would be resolved. The acquisition will be funded through a mixture of Alfa Laval’s cash and existing financing programmes and is expected to be neutral to group margins in the short term. articles.title: Indian ship recycling breakthrough hits Brussels roadblock
articles.summary: A European Parliament committee has voted against allowing two Indian shipbreaking yards onto the EU’s approved recycling list, dealing a setback to shipowners pushing for greater access to South Asian dismantling capacity. The Parliament’s environment committee backed an objection this week to the European...
articles.body: Asia Europe Operations Regulatory Indian ship recycling breakthrough hits Brussels roadblock Adis Ajdin November 6, 2026 2 22,344 2 minutes read Leela Ship Recycling Leela Ship Recycling A European Parliament committee has voted against allowing two Indian shipbreaking yards onto the EU’s approved recycling list, dealing a setback to shipowners pushing for greater access to South Asian dismantling capacity. The Parliament’s environment committee backed an objection this week to the European Commission’s proposal to approve Shree Ram Vessel Scrap and YSI Recyclers, both located in the Alang-Sosiya shipbreaking hub in Gujarat. The two facilities had received preliminary backing from the Commission following inspections intended to establish whether they met the requirements of the EU Ship Recycling Regulation. Their inclusion would make them the first facilities on the Indian subcontinent to join the European list. MEPs opposing the proposal questioned whether yards using the beaching method, in which ships are dismantled on tidal shorelines, could adequately control pollution and hazardous waste. The objection also raised concerns about downstream waste handling, including scrap steel sent to local re-rolling mills that have not been assessed against EU industrial emissions standards. Environmental monitoring cited by campaigners showed elevated levels of toxic substances, including copper, chromium, cadmium and mercury, in the Alang-Sosiya area. “Today’s vote in the European Parliament sends a strong political message to the European Commission,” said Ingvild Jenssen, executive director of NGO Shipbreaking Platform, arguing that approving the facilities despite shortcomings identified during inspections would undermine the regulation’s environmental objectives. The vote puts lawmakers at odds with European shipping interests. Industry association ECSA had urged MEPs to support the Commission’s proposal, arguing that both yards had undergone extensive inspections and had been found compliant with EU standards. ECSA secretary general Sotiris Raptis warned that denying approval to facilities that had passed the assessment process would undermine the credibility of the regulation. Environmental organisations and recycling industry representatives have taken the opposite position, arguing that beaching operations cannot provide sufficient containment of hazardous materials and should not qualify for EU recognition. Campaigners have also challenged the industry’s argument that additional capacity is needed, pointing to more than 2m light displacement tonnes of combined annual capacity at facilities already on the EU list, which they claim is sufficient to handle recent recycling volumes involving EU-flagged and EU-owned ships. Under EU rules, EU-flagged commercial ships subject to the Ship Recycling Regulation must be dismantled at facilities on the approved European list. Opening that list to Indian yards would give owners more recycling options and potentially alter competition with existing approved facilities in Europe and Turkey. The committee vote is not a final rejection. The objection is expected to go before the full European Parliament later in November and does not automatically require the Commission to withdraw its proposal. Member states will also have a say in the approval process. articles.body: Certification & Classification November 6, 2026 · 1 day ago Brazilian field revitalization inches closer with green light for Petrobras’ FPSO concept Petrobras has received the go-ahead from Lloyd’s Register for the conceptual design of its proposed FPSO destined for a redevelopment project. Lloyd’s Register, which awarded approval in principle to Petrobras for the conceptual design of its proposed REVIT I TUPI FPSO unit, describes the AiP as a significant step in the operator’s strategy of leveraging proven offshore production assets to support future field development in Brazil. The approval supports Petrobras' Tupi field revitalization (REVIT I TUPI) project and reflects a growing industry focus on adapting FPSO designs to accelerate project delivery, reduce development risk, and improve capital efficiency. The concept builds on the detailed design of the FPSO P-68, which is currently operating in the Santos Basin. With project costs, delivery schedules, and execution risk under continued scrutiny, the classification society emphasizes that adaptation of existing FPSO designs is emerging as a practical route to bringing new offshore production capacity online while maintaining confidence in safety and performance. " Across the offshore industry, we're seeing growing interest in how proven FPSO designs can be adapted and redeployed to support new developments. Operators are looking for ways to shorten project timelines, reduce complexity and build on existing operational experience. The concept incorporates a comprehensive suite of process engineering documentation, including process flow diagrams, piping and instrumentation diagrams, equipment specifications, and supporting technical studies. LR's review also examined the methodology for managing design modifications, ensuring that changes from the original FPSO P-68 configuration can be identified, assessed, and implemented throughout the project lifecycle.
